author: qurren
headline: Agents quant trade to pay for their own AI subscriptions
summary: Their $200 ChatGPT and $200 Claude plans are paid for by agents that quant trade; leftover tokens go to building things.
evidence: $200 ChatGPT + $200 Claude, I don't pay for it, agents quant trade and pay for their own subscriptions. I then use the rest of the tokens to build stuff.

author: matthiasforstr
headline: Agent's helpful stream check stole the TV account's only connection
summary: Claude Code drives a real Samsung TV; its pre-playback URL check used up the account's single connection, so the player was refused.
evidence: It added a "quick check" of a stream URL before playback, which looked like good practice, but the account allowed one connection, so the check took the slot and the player got refused. Things like that only show up on the hardware.

author: swiftcoder
headline: DeepSeek Flash and KiCad produced working PCBs with minimal prompting
summary: With DeepSeek Flash, KiCad and autorouting they got a couple of working PCBs and a customized ZMK firmware for custom input devices.
evidence: DeepSeek Flash with kicad + autorouting churned out a couple of working PCBs with minimal prompting, and customized ZMK itself for some custom input devices.

author: teekert
headline: Home Hermes agent automates news and job scans for under 3 euros
summary: A Hermes agent on a NUC scans for projects, parses security RSS and builds a searchable notes archive, costing under three euros a month on DeepSeek.
evidence: Most things it makes are LLMs out of the loop, just automations build from simple Unix-style tools that I could have made myself but never took the time for. It's also nice that it solves edge cases itself. It burns less then €3 a month on deepseek or so (just processing public data for me). I keep it on a separate vlan and away from important stuff.

author: jedisct1
headline: Signal-controlled local agent fixed an open source bug from the bus
summary: Initially excited by NBClaw over Signal, they used it less over time, though it still sends HN digests and once fixed a bug while they commuted.
evidence: But eventually, I used it less and less. Nowadays, I still enjoy the fact that it's sending me a summary of cool things it found in Hacker News and research papers on topics I'm interesting in. But that's pretty much it. I don't use it much for agentic tasks anymore. It still happens (I recently used it to fix a bug in an opensource project while I was on the bus), but mostly just only when I ran out of Perplexity Computer credits.

author: KronisLV
headline: Tracking an ALL-CAPS-SWEARING per session metric for coding agents
summary: Despite instructions, memories and linters, their count of all-caps swearing per agent session stays higher than they'd expect from a reliable assistant.
evidence: My ALL-CAPS-SWEARING/SESSION metric is still higher than I'd expect from a reliable assistant system, despite agent instructions and memories and custom tools and linters and all that. In a word, even SOTA models still do stupid shit and bog down workable designs with complexities and mechanisms and concerns that nobody fucking needs.

author: x3haloed
headline: A PR is waiting before they even open the change request
summary: Once 5.6-Sol plus skill files stopped wrecking the codebase, they built a workflow where an agent produces a PR as soon as a change is requested.
evidence: That unlocked a new workflow: as soon as a change is requested, a coding agent reads it and gives me a PR. I want a complete proposed code change in front of my eyeballs by the time I open the change request myself.

author: tcdent
headline: Paying for three Claude Ultra accounts to get enough Fable
summary: They run three Claude Ultra accounts mainly to get enough Fable usage for real development work.
evidence: 1. Claude Ultra, three accounts. Mostly to get enough Fable usage.

author: ddxv
headline: VSCode plus OpenRouter cheap models for about five dollars a month
summary: Using VSCode with OpenRouter and whatever cheap model is current, they spend roughly $5 a month.
evidence: I spend about $5 a month with this setup.
